key_reasoning.reason: New shared core utility (src/codemie/core/header_decoding.py) is threaded into the LiteLLM proxy router, the CLI analytics ingest router/service/postgres gate, the metrics router, and the skill-events router/service — one utility, but consumed from 4+ distinct call sites across API, service, and persistence layers.

decode_attribution_header follows a well-established pattern (stdlib unquote with per-segment fallback and tests), but its output feeds the CLI analytics project authorization gate (cli_analytics_project_gate.py) and attribution used for budget tracking in proxy_router.py — an incorrect decode could silently change which project/budget a request is attributed to. A follow-up commit ("Fix review findings") confirms review surfaced real issues after the first pass.

diffstat reports 17 files changed (612 insertions, 31 deletions): 1 new core module + 6 modified production call sites + ~10 test files touched/added, spanning multiple directories (core, enterprise/litellm, repository/cli_analytics, rest_api/routers, service).

Touches API routers (cli_analytics, metrics, skill_events), Service layer (skill_event_service, cli_analytics_project_gate), DB-Persistence (postgres ingestor attribution), and the External/Integration-facing LiteLLM proxy router — four distinct layers coordinated around one decoding contract, though no schema migration was needed.
